requirements.quote:
The receiving part of a stream initiated by a peer (types 1 and 3 for
   a client, or 0 and 2 for a server) is created when the first STREAM,
   STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, or RESET_STREAM frame is received for that
   stream.  For bidirectional streams initiated by a peer, receipt of a
   MAX_STREAM_DATA or STOP_SENDING frame for the sending part of the
   stream also creates the receiving part.  The initial state for the
   receiving part of a stream is "Recv".
requirements.condition: The first STREAM, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, or RESET_STREAM frame is received for a peer-initiated stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Create the receiving part of the stream.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver each triggering frame for a previously uncreated peer-initiated stream and observe whether its receiving part is created.

requirements.quote:
The receiving part of a stream initiated by a peer (types 1 and 3 for
   a client, or 0 and 2 for a server) is created when the first STREAM,
   STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, or RESET_STREAM frame is received for that
   stream.  For bidirectional streams initiated by a peer, receipt of a
   MAX_STREAM_DATA or STOP_SENDING frame for the sending part of the
   stream also creates the receiving part.  The initial state for the
   receiving part of a stream is "Recv".
requirements.condition: A MAX_STREAM_DATA or STOP_SENDING frame for the sending part of a peer-initiated bidirectional stream is received.
requirements.required_behavior: Create the receiving part of the stream.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send either frame for an uncreated peer-initiated bidirectional stream and inspect receiving-part creation.

requirements.quote:
The receiving part of a stream initiated by a peer (types 1 and 3 for
   a client, or 0 and 2 for a server) is created when the first STREAM,
   STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, or RESET_STREAM frame is received for that
   stream.  For bidirectional streams initiated by a peer, receipt of a
   MAX_STREAM_DATA or STOP_SENDING frame for the sending part of the
   stream also creates the receiving part.  The initial state for the
   receiving part of a stream is "Recv".
requirements.condition: The receiving part of a stream is created.
requirements.required_behavior: Set its initial state to "Recv".
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not initialize it in another receiving state.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's state immediately after creation can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
For a bidirectional stream, the receiving part enters the "Recv"
   state when the sending part initiated by the endpoint (type 0 for a
   client, type 1 for a server) enters the "Ready" state.
requirements.condition: The locally initiated sending part of a bidirectional stream enters the "Ready" state.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the receiving part in the "Recv" state.
requirements.why_checkable: A state-transition test can create a local bidirectional stream and inspect the paired receiving state.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint opens a bidirectional stream when a MAX_STREAM_DATA or
   STOP_SENDING frame is received from the peer for that stream.
requirements.condition: A MAX_STREAM_DATA or STOP_SENDING frame is received from the peer for a bidirectional stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the bidirectional stream as opened.
requirements.why_checkable: Stream-open state is observable after either frame is processed.

requirements.quote:
Before a stream is created, all streams of the same type with lower-
   numbered stream IDs MUST be created.  This ensures that the creation
   order for streams is consistent on both endpoints.
requirements.condition: An endpoint is about to create a stream.
requirements.required_behavior: First create every stream of the same type with a lower-numbered stream ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not create the stream while any lower-numbered stream of the same type remains uncreated.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can trigger creation of a higher-numbered stream and verify that all intervening lower-numbered streams of that type exist first.

requirements.quote:
In the "Recv" state, the endpoint receives STREAM and
   STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames.  Incoming data is buffered and can be
   reassembled into the correct order for delivery to the application.
requirements.condition: The receiving part is in the "Recv" state and STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames arrive.
requirements.required_behavior: Accept and process those frame types in this state.
requirements.why_checkable: Focused tests can inject both frame types while the receiving part is in "Recv" and observe processing.

requirements.quote:
In the "Recv" state, the endpoint receives STREAM and
   STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames.  Incoming data is buffered and can be
   reassembled into the correct order for delivery to the application.
requirements.condition: Stream data arrives out of order while the receiving part is in the "Recv" state.
requirements.required_behavior: Buffer the incoming data and permit reassembly into the correct delivery order.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver offset-bearing data out of order and verify ordered application delivery.

requirements.quote:
As data is consumed by the application and buffer space becomes
   available, the endpoint sends MAX_STREAM_DATA frames to allow the
   peer to send more data.
requirements.condition: The application consumes stream data and receive-buffer space becomes available.
requirements.required_behavior: Send MAX_STREAM_DATA frames to grant the peer additional stream flow-control credit.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can consume buffered data and observe whether the endpoint advertises additional stream credit.

requirements.quote:
When a STREAM frame with a FIN bit is received, the final size of the
   stream is known; see Section 4.5.  The receiving part of the stream
   then enters the "Size Known" state.  In this state, the endpoint no
   longer needs to send MAX_STREAM_DATA frames; it only receives any
   retransmissions of stream data.
requirements.condition: A STREAM frame with the FIN bit is received.
requirements.required_behavior: Record the stream's final size and transition the receiving part to the "Size Known" state.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can process a FIN-bearing STREAM frame and inspect both final-size knowledge and receiving state.

requirements.quote:
When a STREAM frame with a FIN bit is received, the final size of the
   stream is known; see Section 4.5.  The receiving part of the stream
   then enters the "Size Known" state.  In this state, the endpoint no
   longer needs to send MAX_STREAM_DATA frames; it only receives any
   retransmissions of stream data.
requirements.condition: The receiving part is in the "Size Known" state.
requirements.required_behavior: Receive retransmissions of stream data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not treat newly arriving stream data as anything other than retransmission data.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame handling can be inspected after the final size becomes known.

requirements.quote:
Once all data for the stream has been received, the receiving part
   enters the "Data Recvd" state.  This might happen as a result of
   receiving the same STREAM frame that causes the transition to "Size
   Known".  After all data has been received, any STREAM or
   STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames for the stream can be discarded.
requirements.condition: All data through the stream's final size has been received.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the receiving part to the "Data Recvd" state.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can complete receipt of all stream bytes and inspect the resulting state.

requirements.quote:
Once all data for the stream has been received, the receiving part
   enters the "Data Recvd" state.  This might happen as a result of
   receiving the same STREAM frame that causes the transition to "Size
   Known".  After all data has been received, any STREAM or
   STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames for the stream can be discarded.
requirements.condition: A single STREAM frame both supplies the final missing data and carries the FIN bit.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the receiving part to reach "Data Recvd" as part of processing that same frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A focused test can make one frame establish final size and complete all data, then inspect the immediate state.

requirements.quote:
Once all data for the stream has been received, the receiving part
   enters the "Data Recvd" state.  This might happen as a result of
   receiving the same STREAM frame that causes the transition to "Size
   Known".  After all data has been received, any STREAM or
   STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames for the stream can be discarded.
requirements.condition: All stream data has already been received and another STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame arrives for that stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the frame to be discarded.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject either frame after complete receipt and verify that discarding it causes no required processing failure.

requirements.quote:
The "Data Recvd" state persists until stream data has been delivered
   to the application.  Once stream data has been delivered, the stream
   enters the "Data Read" state, which is a terminal state.
requirements.condition: The receiving part is in "Data Recvd" and stream data has not yet been delivered to the application.
requirements.required_behavior: Remain in the "Data Recvd" state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not transition to "Data Read" before delivery.
requirements.why_checkable: State can be observed while application delivery is withheld.

requirements.quote:
The "Data Recvd" state persists until stream data has been delivered
   to the application.  Once stream data has been delivered, the stream
   enters the "Data Read" state, which is a terminal state.
requirements.condition: All stream data has been delivered to the application.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream to the terminal "Data Read" state and remain terminal.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not transition out of "Data Read" afterward.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can complete application delivery, inspect the state, and attempt subsequent events to verify terminality.

requirements.quote:
Receiving a RESET_STREAM frame in the "Recv" or "Size Known" state
   causes the stream to enter the "Reset Recvd" state.  This might cause
   the delivery of stream data to the application to be interrupted.
requirements.condition: A RESET_STREAM frame is received while the receiving part is in "Recv" or "Size Known".
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the stream to the "Reset Recvd" state.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject RESET_STREAM in each source state and inspect the destination state.

requirements.quote:
It is possible that all stream data has already been received when a
   RESET_STREAM is received (that is, in the "Data Recvd" state).
   Similarly, it is possible for remaining stream data to arrive after
   receiving a RESET_STREAM frame (the "Reset Recvd" state).  An
   implementation is free to manage this situation as it chooses.
requirements.condition: Remaining stream data arrives after RESET_STREAM has placed the stream in "Reset Recvd".
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the implementation to manage or receive the remaining data according to its chosen strategy.
requirements.why_checkable: Runtime tests can deliver remaining stream data after RESET_STREAM and verify that the implementation follows a consistent supported strategy.

requirements.quote:
Sending a RESET_STREAM means that an endpoint cannot guarantee
   delivery of stream data; however, there is no requirement that stream
   data not be delivered if a RESET_STREAM is received.  An
   implementation MAY interrupt delivery of stream data, discard any
   data that was not consumed, and signal the receipt of the
   RESET_STREAM.
requirements.condition: A RESET_STREAM is received.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit interruption of stream-data delivery.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can receive RESET_STREAM during delivery and verify that interruption is an allowed implementation outcome.

requirements.quote:
Sending a RESET_STREAM means that an endpoint cannot guarantee
   delivery of stream data; however, there is no requirement that stream
   data not be delivered if a RESET_STREAM is received.  An
   implementation MAY interrupt delivery of stream data, discard any
   data that was not consumed, and signal the receipt of the
   RESET_STREAM.
requirements.condition: A RESET_STREAM is received while some stream data remains unconsumed.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit discarding the unconsumed data.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can leave data unconsumed, receive RESET_STREAM, and observe whether the implementation elects to discard it.

requirements.quote:
Sending a RESET_STREAM means that an endpoint cannot guarantee
   delivery of stream data; however, there is no requirement that stream
   data not be delivered if a RESET_STREAM is received.  An
   implementation MAY interrupt delivery of stream data, discard any
   data that was not consumed, and signal the receipt of the
   RESET_STREAM.
requirements.condition: A RESET_STREAM is received.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit signaling receipt of RESET_STREAM to the application.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can receive RESET_STREAM and observe whether the application is notified.

requirements.quote:
Sending a RESET_STREAM means that an endpoint cannot guarantee
   delivery of stream data; however, there is no requirement that stream
   data not be delivered if a RESET_STREAM is received.  An
   implementation MAY interrupt delivery of stream data, discard any
   data that was not consumed, and signal the receipt of the
   RESET_STREAM.
requirements.condition: A RESET_STREAM is received.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit already received stream data to still be delivered.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not impose a requirement that receipt of RESET_STREAM always prevents stream-data delivery.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can receive RESET_STREAM with buffered data and verify that delivering that data is accepted behavior.

requirements.quote:
RESET_STREAM.  A RESET_STREAM signal might be suppressed or withheld
   if stream data is completely received and is buffered to be read by
   the application.  If the RESET_STREAM is suppressed, the receiving
   part of the stream remains in "Data Recvd".
requirements.condition: Stream data is completely received and buffered for the application when RESET_STREAM is received.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the RESET_STREAM signal to be suppressed or withheld.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can fully buffer a stream, receive RESET_STREAM, and observe whether application reset notification is withheld.

requirements.quote:
RESET_STREAM.  A RESET_STREAM signal might be suppressed or withheld
   if stream data is completely received and is buffered to be read by
   the application.  If the RESET_STREAM is suppressed, the receiving
   part of the stream remains in "Data Recvd".
requirements.condition: The RESET_STREAM signal is suppressed.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the receiving part in the "Data Recvd" state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not transition the receiving part to "Reset Recvd" or "Reset Read" solely for the suppressed signal.
requirements.why_checkable: The receiving state can be inspected after choosing to suppress reset notification.

requirements.quote:
Once the application receives the signal indicating that the stream
   was reset, the receiving part of the stream transitions to the "Reset
   Read" state, which is a terminal state.
requirements.condition: The application receives the signal that the stream was reset.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition the receiving part to the terminal "Reset Read" state and remain terminal.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not transition out of "Reset Read" afterward.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver the reset signal to the application, inspect the state, and verify that later events do not leave it.
